habitat: Clear, still inland waters with waterlilies and pondweed, and some emergent grass or reeds, including quiet pans, dams and pools. It also uses temporarily flooded grassland.
summary: A tiny goose of lily pans. Newman identifies it by the dark green upperparts, orange body and short yellow bill, with white wing panels in flight. The male has a white face, black eye-patches, a black crown down the nape, green ear-patches and a white collar. Wikipedia describes the male breast and flanks as chestnut and the belly as white. The female has a grey face, a dark brown eye-stripe and a dark brown crown. The immature resembles the female. The male twitters and the female gives a weak quack and a twittering whistle.

similar.note: White-backed Duck shares lily-covered water but is mottled, with a pale spot at the base of a black bill. African Pygmy Goose has a white face, a short yellow bill and an orange body.

bill.shape: short and yellow, with a black tip

head.pattern: Wikipedia: white face, black eye-patches, an iridescent black crown down the nape, powder-green ear-patches and a white collar on the upper neck.

underparts.pattern: Newman calls the body orange and the summary line orange-beige. Wikipedia names the male lower neck, breast and flanks chestnut, and the belly white.

wings.pattern: White wing panels are diagnostic in flight. Wikipedia: black wings, metallic green coverts and a white bar on the outer secondaries.

head.pattern: Wikipedia: a grey face, a dark brown eye-stripe, smudged brown cheeks and nape, and a dark brown forehead, crown and nape. The female breast and flanks were not in the text used here.

wings.pattern: Newman gives the white wing panels as a species mark in flight.

head.pattern: Newman says the immature resembles the female.

viewNotes.note: Male: a white face, green ear-patch, black crown and short yellow bill on an orange body. The bird sits low among lilies.
The male white face and black eye-patch are the front pattern. The bill is short and yellow with a black tip.
The upperparts are dark green. The white wing panel is hidden at rest.
White panels on the wing are the flight mark.
The underwing is not given a separate colour in these texts.
The female face is grey, with a dark brown eye-stripe and a dark brown crown. Newman does not describe a separate female body colour.
Newman says the immature resembles the female.

calls.description: A soft twittering whistle, choo-choo or pee-wee, and a repeated subdued tsu-tswi.
A weak quack and a twittering whistle.
The sexed calls are from Newman. The catalogue cut is not labelled male or female. Grade A, Ethiopia. Lake Awassa, Ethiopia. No playable southern African grade A file outranked it.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. SABAP1 names the Limpopo floodplain in northern Kruger as a Transvaal locality and says local numbers follow waterlily growth rather than a regional migration. The female body colours were cut off in the Wikipedia text, so they were left empty. Chick down, a female photograph and the underwing were not found. The call is grade A from Ethiopia and is not sexed. Newman’s orange body and Wikipedia’s chestnut male underparts are both cited.
